answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a per-identity bond that is slashed on misbehavior. To join, an agent locks collateral at the registry, so each extra identity needs fresh capital: the bond is a hard ridge between fake wallets, not a soft gate. The registry also requires a signed attestation renewed each epoch, with an onyx-hard proof of work behind it, and it keeps an ivory-clean public list of stakes and slashes. A Sybil cluster pays the deposit plus renewal compute per head, and one detected fake can burn the whole stake, making mass identity far costlier than honest work.
